text: Cherubim are winged heavenly beings who stand guard near God.
The tree in the middle of the Garden of Eden, a symbol of unending life. After sin, the way to this tree was closed to humankind.
The Spirit of God. Christians confess him, together with the Father and the Son, as the one God.
The love and gifts God freely gives to people who have done nothing to deserve them.
To become pregnant with a child. Mary carried her child not through a man but by the Holy Spirit.
A count of the population ordered by the Roman emperor for taxation. Everyone had to go to their ancestral town to be listed.
A trough that holds feed for horses or cattle. It was the first bed of the infant Jesus.
One who saves; here, the one who rescues people from sin and death.
A rite in which the foreskin of a baby boy was cut on the eighth day after birth. It was the sign of God's covenant with his people.
A rite under the law for making a person or thing clean. After giving birth, a mother brought an offering once a set number of days had passed.
The teaching and commandments God gave Israel through Moses, recorded in the first five books of the Old Testament.
The great building in Jerusalem where people worshiped God and offered sacrifices. The temple of Jesus' day had been lavishly rebuilt by Herod.
A Greek word meaning 'anointed one', the same as the Hebrew 'Messiah'. It refers to the Savior God promised to send.
A Hebrew word meaning 'anointed one': the promised Savior Israel was waiting for. In Greek the word is 'Christ'.
One of the twelve clans of Israel, descended from the twelve sons of Jacob.
A person who receives God's word and passes it on to others. Their main task was making God's will known, more than foretelling the future.
Going without food for a time in order to focus on prayer.
Not men with academic degrees, but scholars from the East who studied the stars. They likely came from Persia or Babylon.
The head of the priests and the highest religious leader, in charge of the temple and the Jewish council.
A man who offered sacrifices in the temple and came before God on behalf of the people. The office belonged to the descendants of Aaron.
A member of the tribe of Levi, who assisted the priests with the work of the temple.
An expert who studied and taught the law. Older translations call them 'scribes'.
To bow down and honor someone as highest; the deepest expression of reverence, given to God or to a king.
A precious resin from a tree that gives off a sweet smell when burned. It was used in offerings to God.
A costly spice taken from tree resin, used as medicine and perfume and also to prepare bodies for burial.
A spice from a strongly fragrant wood, mixed with myrrh and used on bodies at burial.
Not just feeling sorry for wrongs, but turning one's whole life around and coming back to God.
A rite of being immersed in or washed with water, showing that sins are washed away and a new life begins.
The chief of the evil spirits, who opposes God and tries to make people fall. 'Satan' means 'adversary'.
Recalling the young lambs offered as sacrifices for sin, this title points to Jesus, who would die bearing the sin of the world.
A Hebrew word meaning 'my teacher', a respectful title for a teacher of the law. 'Rabboni' is a warmer form.
A miracle that shows God's power and points to who Jesus is.
Merchants who exchanged money from many lands for the coins used in the temple, charging a fee for their profit.
Meaning 'son of a human being', the name Jesus most often used for himself. It recalls the heavenly ruler in the book of Daniel.
A Jewish group devoted to keeping the law and the traditions of the elders in every detail. They often clashed with Jesus.
People of Samaria, the region between Judea and Galilee. They and the Jews had long been hostile and avoided each other.
Hours were counted from about sunrise, so the seventh hour is around one in the afternoon.
The seventh day of the week, a holy day for resting from work and remembering God. It ran from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday.
The place in each town where Jews gathered to read Scripture, pray, and learn.
The person who led the gatherings and worship of a synagogue.
A book made of long strips of leather or papyrus joined and rolled up. The Scriptures were written this way.
Evil spirits that seize and torment people. Jesus drove them out with a word.
Unable to move the body because of paralysis.
People who collected taxes from their own people for Rome. Many took extra for themselves, so they were treated as sinners.
A long walkway with a roof held up by columns, open on one or both sides.
Meaning 'one who is sent', the title of the twelve disciples Jesus chose and appointed.
A member of a Jewish movement that sought to drive out Roman rule, even by force.
Broad, solid stone, a picture of a foundation that cannot be shaken. The name Peter also means 'stone' or 'rock'.
A small room deep inside a house; a place to pray alone, away from others' eyes.
A Roman officer in command of about a hundred soldiers.
Older leaders who guided a town or the people.
A precious fragrant oil. Nard was a very costly perfume made from a plant grown in the Himalayas.
A smooth stone jar for holding perfume. Its neck was broken so it could be poured out all at once.
A Roman silver coin, about a day's wage for a laborer.
Here, a debt that is reduced or wiped out so it no longer has to be repaid.
The back part of a boat. The front is called the bow.
An illness in which bleeding does not stop. Under the law it made a person unclean, cutting them off from others.
The food God sent down from heaven every day during Israel's forty years in the wilderness.
'Greek' here means a non-Jewish person shaped by Greek culture. Gentiles are peoples other than the Jews, and their lands.
A seven-day autumn festival after the harvest, when people lived in shelters made of branches to remember the wilderness years.
Small temporary huts woven from branches or grass.
Sexual relations between a married person and someone other than their spouse. The law punished it severely.
To declare someone guilty and pass sentence on them.
A winter festival remembering how the temple, defiled by a Greek king, was won back and rededicated to God. Today it is called Hanukkah.
Carob pods, mostly used as food for pigs and livestock. Only the very poor would eat them.
Coins made of silver; here drachmas, each worth about a day's wage.
The highest Jewish assembly and court, led by the high priest. It is also called the Sanhedrin.
A dead person coming back to life. The resurrection of Jesus is at the center of the Christian faith.
A teaching God orders his people to keep. The Ten Commandments are the best known.
A fig-like tree with low, wide-spreading branches that is easy to climb.
A serious skin disease. In Bible times it was considered unclean, and those who had it had to live apart outside the village.
A unit of weight; here the Roman litra, about 330 grams.
The date palm. Its branches were waved as a sign of victory and welcome.
A Hebrew word meaning 'save us now', which became a shout of welcome and praise.
Jews who supported the rule of Herod's family and went along with paying taxes to Rome.
A Jewish group close to the high priestly families. They did not believe in the resurrection or in angels.
Trumpet-shaped chests in the temple courts where people put their offerings.
A unit for a large sum of money, about what a laborer earned in nearly twenty years. The English word 'talent' comes from it.
A seven-day festival following Passover, when people ate bread without yeast to remember the exodus from Egypt.
The great spring festival remembering the night death passed over Israel's houses in Egypt, and the exodus.
A large room on the upper floor of a house, where Jesus ate his last meal with his disciples.
A binding promise God makes with people. Jesus established a new covenant with his own blood.
A song in praise of God. At the end of the Passover meal, psalms were sung.
An official sent by the Roman emperor to rule a province. Pilate was governor of Judea.
The wooden frame on which Rome hung condemned prisoners to die; the cruelest and most shameful form of execution.
Purple cloth was costly and worn by kings. The soldiers put it on Jesus to mock him as a king.
The blessed place where the righteous dead are with God.
The heavy curtain in the temple that screened off the Most Holy Place. It stood for the barrier between God and people.
Fine cloth woven from flax, used to wrap the bodies of the dead.
The day after the Sabbath, our Sunday. Jesus rose on this day.
A unit of distance; one stadion is about 185 meters, so sixty stadia is about 11 kilometers.
The night was divided into four watches; the fourth ran from about three to six in the morning.
The power and the right to rule and give commands.
People God accepts as right before him. Here it also pokes at those who consider themselves righteous.
A name for Jerusalem, where God's temple stood.
The realm where God rules as king. It is less a place than God's rule being carried out.
Not just living forever, but the true life shared with God.
What makes dough rise. Jesus used its power, a little spreading through the whole batch, as a picture.
A very tiny seed that grows into a plant taller than a person.
Here, the appointed feasts when Jews went up to Jerusalem, such as Passover and the Feast of Tabernacles.
Aramaic, the language Jews spoke in Jesus' day. 'Talitha koum' means 'little girl, get up', and 'Ephphatha' means 'be opened'.
A price paid to set a captive or slave free. Jesus gave his own life as that price.
A journey to a holy place. At each festival, Jews went up to the temple in Jerusalem.
